addDomainForm.subdomainHint: — recommended, keeps your apex reputation separate
addDomainForm.trackingPreviewExample: For example, your tracking links will use {host}
addDomainForm.streamNote: We recommend one name per kind of mail: {transactionalName} for transactional (receipts, password resets) and {bulkName} for campaigns and lifecycle mail. A subdomain does not inherit your root domain's reputation, so each one needs its own SPF record, its own DKIM key and its own warm-up — which is exactly what keeps a bad campaign away from your password resets. Add them one at a time here; once a domain is added, Owlat generates every record for the whole layout in one pass.
addDomainForm.apexNote: Sending from your apex {zone} shares its sending reputation with everything else that sends from it, and any SPF record it already publishes must be merged into one. When you verify, Owlat shows the single merged record to publish.
addDomainForm.returnPathPreviewExample: For example, bounces would come from {host}
addDomainForm.freemailWarning: You can't publish DNS records for {zone} — it's a shared mailbox provider you don't control. Use a domain you own, or {migrateLink} instead.
addDomainForm.nsWarning: We couldn't find any nameservers for {zone} — double-check the spelling. You can still add it if the domain is brand new and its DNS is still being set up.

SPF allows at most 10 DNS lookups — double-check the merged record stays within that limit.

yahooCflPanel.heading: Yahoo complaint feedback loop
yahooCflPanel.intro: Yahoo reports spam complaints to senders who enroll the DKIM domain they sign with. Enrolling is optional — it measures Yahoo complaints directly instead of standing in for them.

resetConfirmation.ourRecord: • Our record is cleared — the submitted and enrolled dates are lost.
resetConfirmation.yahooRecord: • Yahoo’s own enrollment is untouched. If it is still live, the next Yahoo complaint will not restore this record; re-submit the form step to record it again.
resetConfirmation.fallback: • Yahoo complaint measurement falls back to the unsubscribe-rate proxy — a sharp rise against this cell’s own recent history — with lower confidence.
